lens: Keep finger travel, pinky load, same-hand thumb chords and static holds low for 8+ hours a day of chat and Rust.

support: In keyboard.json, L-outer and R-outer sit 1u closer to the hand than the inner thumb keys. Space (the most frequent tap) and the user's Esc/⇧ therefore get the shortest thumb travel.
OS⇧ is a one-shot key, so capitals typed from the left pinky need no held key. It is the cheapest way to capitalise right-hand letters such as 'I'.

There are only three home-row mods per hand and none on the index fingers, so the fastest fingers never wait on hold logic. With Chordal Hold, ⌘ on D pairs with right-hand letters and ⌘ on K with left-hand letters, so every shortcut is a cross-hand chord.
Leader, Caps Word and the screenshot key are rare enough that a two-row reach to the top row is acceptable.
layers.verdict: Keep it as it is. Its ergonomic costs come from the fixed keys (Bspc in the top-right corner, `=` in the bottom-right corner, ⌃ on the pinkies), and only the tap-hold config can soften them.

support: The left thumb holds while the right index, middle and ring fingers type on a 3x3 numpad. That is cross-hand, and all the digits sit in the strong columns.
With plain ⌃⌥⌘ on A S D, ⌘+digit is thumb + middle finger + one right-hand tap. That is lighter than the old tap dance's timed double tap.
Layer Lock on B removes the static thumb hold during long number entry.
`/` stays in its QWERTY spot and `-` is on the index finger, so paths and CLI flags (`--release`) can be typed without leaving the layer.

changes.key: Numbers + IDE, R-outer thumb (base R-outer is unchanged)
changes.why: 0 is the most-used digit in code (0, 10, 0x00, [0]), and N is the index finger's worst spot (sideways and down). The right thumb is free on this layer, nothing here needs Esc or Shift, and R-inner stays transparent for the tri-layer; keep 0 on N as well while the user adapts.

changes.key: Numbers + IDE, left bottom, C position
changes.why: The command palette is the most-used shortcut on this layer, and on Z it is the widest same-hand span: the pinky goes down to the bottom row while the thumb holds the inner key. On C it is a middle-finger tap, and 'C for Command palette' is still mnemonic.

changes.key: Numbers + IDE, left bottom, Z position
changes.why: Copy path is rare, so it can take the pinky slot, and it sits next to Copy relative path on X.

layers.verdict: This is a good layer. Move 0 onto the free right thumb and move the palette off the pinky.

support: With SYM on the right thumb, the fixed left half (`( ) [ ] < > ! & ? #`, most of Rust's symbols) is now cross-hand instead of same-hand.
Moving SYM off Space takes Flow Tap out of the symbol path. `my_var` and `␣{` no longer misfire.
The `->` and `=>` macros on the index and middle top row turn two-key symbol sequences into a single chord.
With no duplicates, each symbol has exactly one finger path, which cuts down on hesitation and correction keystrokes.
layers.verdict: Keep it. The remaining cost is that `_ { } " ->` are same-hand with the right thumb, which the fixed left half makes unavoidable.

support: The arrows sit opposite the holding thumb and ⌃⌥⌘⇧ are on the left home row. Selection (Space + F + arrows) is then a chord with both hands at rest and no reaching.
Undo, Cut, Copy and Paste on Z X C V copy the Mac ⌘ posture and need only the thumb, not a home-row mod plus a letter.
With the VS Code and media keys gone, every Nav key is within one row of home.
Enter on R-inner confirms a menu item without the right hand leaving the arrows. Del on the Bspc key matches the Mac's fn+⌫.

changes.why: Reading code, scrolling diffs and long selections otherwise keep the left thumb held for minutes at a time. G is a sideways index reach, which suits a rare key, and it is in the same column as LLock on Numbers (B).

layers.verdict: Lean and well placed. Add Layer Lock so that long navigation is not a static thumb hold.

support: The F-keys mirror the numpad, so there is no new map to learn. Holding both reach thumbs is acceptable for occasional keys.
With ⇧⌘⌥⌃ on the right home row, ⇧F12 and ⌥F12 are cross-hand chords.
Boot and Lock sit in the corners behind a two-thumb hold, which makes them very hard to hit by accident.

changes.why: Without it, a debug session (F10 step over, F11 step into, F5 continue) means holding both inner thumbs while the pinky reaches F10 and F11. It needs the C guard in the config section so the tri-layer does not turn off a locked F layer.

layers.verdict: Fine for occasional use. Add Layer Lock for bursts of debugging.

support: Each thumb carries one layer hold plus one other role. The long holds are split (NAV on the left, SYM on the right), so neither thumb holds all day.
Space and Esc/⇧ are on the home thumb keys. A NUM tap that leaks through is a harmless newline, and a leaked SYM tap is a Tab, not a sent message.
Real Enter (hold Space + tap R-inner) is a two-thumb chord across both hands, so neither hand strains. With permissive hold it is also fast.
concerns: SYM is the busiest hold for Rust, and it sits on R-inner, which is 1u further toward the centre and 0.25u lower than R-outer. The thumb therefore stretches for every symbol, so watch for soreness at the base of the thumb.

Every message send is a two-thumb chord. Flow Tap also makes Space a tap if it comes within 150 ms of the last letter, which gives ' ' + Tab instead of Enter, so the user must pause briefly before sending.
Some same-hand thumb+finger chords remain: Shift + right-hand capitals (prefer OS⇧ for 'I'), SYM + `_ { } "`, NUM + the IDE keys, and NAV + the clipboard keys.
The F layer needs both reach thumbs held at once. That is fine for rare keys, and it is why the layer needs Layer Lock.

config: CHORDAL_HOLD with an explicit chordal_hold_layout: 'L' and 'R' for the letter keys and '*' for all four thumb keys. Every thumb has same-hand content (Shift + 'I', SYM + `{`, NAV + ⌘C, NUM + IDE keys), and without '*' those chords resolve as taps, for example Esc + i.
PERMISSIVE_HOLD globally, which the QMK docs recommend together with Chordal Hold. A key pressed and released inside a hold counts as a chord at once, while rolls stay taps.

HOLD_ON_OTHER_KEY_PRESS_PER_KEY, returning true only for the SYM/Tab thumb. A rolled symbol should never leak a Tab, which moves focus in Slack and browsers, and Tab almost never overlaps the next key.

TAPPING_TERM 200 with TAPPING_TERM_PER_KEY: 150 for Esc/⇧, 230 for the ring and pinky home-row mods (A, S, L, :), and 200 for the rest. A slow Esc that becomes a lone Shift is harmless, but a rolled capital that leaks Esc can stop a Claude Code run; ring and pinky fingers are slower to lift.

QUICK_TAP_TERM_PER_KEY: 0 for all four thumbs, so Tab-to-accept then `(`, newline then `1.`, and Esc then ⇧A in Vim give the hold instead of auto-repeat. Use 120 for the home-row mods so that holding `l` in Vim still repeats.

FLOW_TAP_TERM 150 with a get_flow_tap_term that returns 0 for the ⇧⏎/NUM key. Oryx dual-function keys are LT(layer, letter) (DUAL_FUNC_0 is LT(3, KC_X)), so the default would treat NUM as a letter and type a newline instead of activating NUM after 'v' or '␣'. Keep 150 for Space and the home-row mods, and drop Space to 120 if sent messages come out as ' ' + Tab.
(C) In layer_state_set_user, call update_tri_layer_state(state, NUM, SYM, FKEYS) only when !is_layer_locked(FKEYS). Otherwise, releasing the thumbs turns off a locked F layer.

DOUBLE_TAP_SHIFT_TURNS_ON_CAPS_WORD: the firmware accepts OSM(MOD_LSFT) for this, and ONESHOT_TAP_TOGGLE is unset, so there is no conflict. Double-tapping the left OS⇧ then starts SCREAMING_CASE without the two-row reach to the CW key.
warnings: The right pinky is the most heavily loaded finger: Bspc in the top-right corner (fixed), then ', :/⌃, ; and P, and `=` in the bottom corner, which is the pinky's worst spot for a key Rust uses constantly. Pain on the outer forearm (little-finger side) is the first sign to watch for.

⌃ on both pinkies (A and :) carries Vim's ⌃D, ⌃U, ⌃W and ⌃O plus the terminal's ⌃C and ⌃R. Long pinky holds are a classic RSI route, so keep them short and use the opposite-hand pinky, which Chordal Hold enforces.

`_` in snake_case is the most repeated symbol in Rust, and it is now a same-hand chord: the right thumb on the reach key plus a sideways index reach to H. If the right thumb or index finger gets sore, move `_` first.
`"` sits on the outer pinky key while the right thumb holds the inner key, which is the widest same-hand span on the board. OS⇧ then `'` is a cross-hand alternative.
Quick fix (⌘. on Q) is a pinky top-row reach while the thumb is on the inner key. For Rust's frequent quick fixes, holding D (⌘) on Base and tapping `.` is cross-hand and easier.
Selecting by word on Nav (Space + ⌥ on S + ⇧ on F + arrows) holds three keys at once on the left hand. That is fine in short bursts but tiring during long refactors.
Expect 2 to 3 weeks of slower, tenser typing while the new thumb roles settle. That tension is a strain risk in itself, so take breaks and don't push for speed.
